verses.1: To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David.
verses.2: Rescue me, O LORD, from the wicked man; deliver me from the violent man.
verses.3: Those who plot evil in their heart, all day they prepare for battle.
verses.4: Their tongues are sharpened like a serpent; the poison of an adder is under their lips. Selah.
verses.5: Keep me, O LORD, from the hand of the wicked; deliver me from the violent man who plots to trip up my steps.
verses.6: The arrogant have set a trap for me; they have spread a net of ropes beneath my feet, and set pitfalls for me. Selah.
verses.7: I said to the LORD who is my God, “Hear, O LORD, the sound of my plea.”
verses.8: O Lord, the LORD, my strength, my salvation, you have covered my head in the day of battle.
verses.9: Let not the wicked man’s desire be fulfilled, O LORD, let them not imagine triumph. Selah.
verses.10: Let the head of those who surround me be covered with the toil of their own lips.
verses.11: Let burning coals fall upon them, let them be cast down with distress and not rise again.
verses.12: Let a lying tongue not be established on the earth, let a violent man seek no advantage.
verses.13: I know that the LORD will do justice for the afflicted, and will render judgment for the poor.
verses.14: But the righteous will give thanks to your name; the upright will dwell in your presence.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: "the poison of an adder" — the Hebrew uses *hamat 'achshuv*, literally "poison of an adder," which is a rare compound. The translation follows the literal meaning rather than seeking a more general equivalent.
- v. 9: "let them not imagine triumph" — the Hebrew uses *al tafek yarumu*, which is translated with a slight interpretive choice to render the nuance of "imagine triumph" instead of a more literal "do not lift up."
- v. 12: "let a violent man seek no advantage" — the Hebrew uses *madhephet*, which can mean "advantage" or "profit," and is rendered here to match the moral tone of the psalm.

[1] To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David.

[2] Rescue me, O LORD, from the wicked man; deliver me from the violent man.

[3] Those who plot evil in their heart, all day they prepare for battle.

[4] Their tongues are sharpened like a serpent; the poison of an adder is under their lips. Selah.

[5] Keep me, O LORD, from the hand of the wicked; deliver me from the violent man who plots to trip up my steps.

[6] The arrogant have set a trap for me; they have spread a net of ropes beneath my feet, and set pitfalls for me. Selah.

[7] I said to the LORD who is my God, “Hear, O LORD, the sound of my plea.”

[8] O Lord, the LORD, my strength, my salvation, you have covered my head in the day of battle.

[9] Let not the wicked man’s desire be fulfilled, O LORD, let them not imagine triumph. Selah.

[10] Let the head of those who surround me be covered with the toil of their own lips.

[11] Let burning coals fall upon them, let them be cast down with distress and not rise again.

[12] Let a lying tongue not be established on the earth, let a violent man seek no advantage.

[13] I know that the LORD will do justice for the afflicted, and will render judgment for the poor.

[14] But the righteous will give thanks to your name; the upright will dwell in your presence.

Notes
- v. 4: "the poison of an adder" — the Hebrew uses *hamat 'achshuv*, literally "poison of an adder," which is a rare compound. The translation follows the literal meaning rather than seeking a more general equivalent.
- v. 9: "let them not imagine triumph" — the Hebrew uses *al tafek yarumu*, which is translated with a slight interpretive choice to render the nuance of "imagine triumph" instead of a more literal "do not lift up."
- v. 12: "let a violent man seek no advantage" — the Hebrew uses *madhephet*, which can mean "advantage" or "profit," and is rendered here to match the moral tone of the psalm.
